Write an image

Source: R/write.R
pix_write.Rd

pix_write() picks the format from file's extension (or format) and passes ... to that format's writer. The writers take the shapes pix_read() returns:

Usage

pix_write(x, file, format = NULL, ...)

pix_write_png(
  x,
  file = NULL,
  bits = NULL,
  compression = 6L,
  icc = NULL,
  exif = NULL,
  srgb = NULL
)

pix_write_qoi(x, file = NULL, colourspace = c("srgb", "linear"))

Arguments

x

The image.

file

A path to write, or NULL to return the encoded bytes.

format

NULL to use file's extension, or "png" or "qoi".

...

Arguments for the format's writer.

bits

NULL keeps the image's depth (8 for doubles and nativeRasters); 8L or 16L forces it.

compression

The zlib level, 0 (store) to 9 (smallest).

icc

An ICC profile as a raw vector, written as iCCP.

exif

An EXIF block (TIFF header onward) as a raw vector, written as eXIf.

srgb

NULL, or the sRGB chunk's rendering intent: 0 perceptual, 1 relative colorimetric, 2 saturation, 3 absolute colorimetric. PNG does not allow both icc and srgb.

colourspace

The QOI header's colourspace byte: "srgb" or "linear". It is a label only; pixels are written as given.

Value

With file, file, invisibly; with file = NULL, a raw vector.

Details

  • a nativeRaster (8-bit RGBA);

  • a double array or matrix with values in [0, 1], clamped to that range and rounded to bits;

  • an integer array or matrix of sample values. Its bits attribute gives the depth; without one it is 8-bit if every value is at most 255.

A matrix is a grey image; a height x width x channels array has 1 to 4 channels (grey, grey and alpha, RGB, RGBA). NA is an error.

Functions

  • pix_write_png(): PNG at 8 or 16 bits, 1 to 4 channels, with an optional ICC profile, EXIF block or sRGB rendering intent.

  • pix_write_qoi(): QOI, 8-bit RGB or RGBA; grey widens to RGB.

See also

pix_read(), and zupix-conditions for the errors raised.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "gradient.png", package = "zupix")
img <- pix_read(f, as = "integer")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".qoi")
pix_write(img, out)
identical(pix_read(out, as = "integer"), img)
#> [1] TRUE
